text:
Timo Meier is doing almost everything right except scoring. He has 80 shots in 21 games and 7.7 expected goals (a measure of the quality of his chances). He has four goals. That's 5% shooting against a range of 8% to 12% for him, and his line has also scored 4.8 fewer goals than its chances deserve.

That's the textbook definition of due. His two-goal night in Toronto on Nov. 8 and a power-play goal from the net front in Washington on Nov. 14 hinted at the turn, and his chance rate has held steady with last season.

The style hasn't changed either. He hits (36 already), his speed bursts rank in the 93rd percentile by NHL EDGE, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 87th percentile for chances from in front of the net, carrying the puck in on 54% of his entries. On a team that has won eight of its last ten, nine points is a quiet line for a player shooting this much. Keep watching the shot totals. The goals usually follow.
